property_summary: Setting the blacklist status of an address and then transferring at least 1 token from a blacklisted address (with the other party not blacklisted) must revert, because blacklisted senders cannot transfer.
A transfer from a blacklisted address (to a non-blacklisted recipient) always reverts.
A transferOut of tokens from a blacklisted address (to a non-blacklisted recipient) always reverts, because blacklisted senders cannot transfer.
A transferFrom from a blacklisted address to a non-blacklisted recipient always reverts, regardless of the caller's allowance, because blacklisted senders cannot transfer.
Setting a non-zero address as blacklisted and then having that blacklisted address call transfer directly to a non-blacklisted recipient always reverts.

Setting a new liquidity receive address and marking it white lets it transfer tokens like a whitelisted account, i.e., its transfer of a positive amount from a funded address succeeds and returns true.

property_summary: After the owner transfers ownership to a non-zero address, that new owner is c.owner(), and setting the caller role to an arbitrary address succeeds and makes that address usable for caller-gated functions.
After the owner transfers ownership to a non-zero address, that new owner becomes c.owner(), and a subsequent caller-gated function can be invoked by setting a caller via setCaller.
After the owner transfers ownership to a non-zero address, that address becomes c.owner(), and a caller set by the new owner can invoke caller-gated functions such as setCfg.
After the owner transfers ownership to a non-zero address, that address becomes the owner, and a caller set by the new owner can invoke setCfg.
